title: Pokemon LeafGreen Version
sources: pret/pokefirered decompilation (GitHub; builds FireRed and LeafGreen): trainer parties, map scripts, hidden items (map.json bg_events), in-game trades, Game Corner prizes, evolutions, wild encounters, roamer.c
The English ROM itself (BPGE, Rev 1): region map section names and trainer names/levels, read on the PC with ui/src/pokemon.cpp (findTables) - the ground truth for every place name and level cap

milestones.name: Rival: first battle (Oak's lab)
milestones.tips: Your rival picks the starter strong against yours. Both have only Tackle/Scratch and a stat move at Level 5: just attack.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (RIVAL_OAKS_LAB_*; the player-named rival is stored as TERRY)

milestones.name: Oak's Parcel and the Pokédex
milestones.tips: The Viridian Mart clerk hands you Oak's Parcel. Take it back to Pallet Town: Oak gives you the Pokédex and five Poké Balls, and the old man in Viridian then shows how to catch.
milestones.source: pret/pokefirered ViridianCity_Mart, PalletTown_ProfessorOaksLab scripts

milestones.name: Rival: Route 22 (optional)
milestones.tips: West of Viridian your rival waits with a Pidgey and the starter at 9. It is optional but good experience; there is no gym in Viridian yet.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (RIVAL_ROUTE22_EARLY_*)

milestones.name: Gym 1: Brock
milestones.badge_note: Boulder Badge: Flash works in the field (HM05 from Oak's aide on Route 2 once you have 10 species). Gym TM: TM39 Rock Tomb.
milestones.tips: Geodude 12 and Onix 14 (Rock/Ground). Bulbasaur and Squirtle win; Charmander learns Metal Claw at 13, or catch a Mankey on Route 22 or a Butterfree with Confusion in Viridian Forest.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h; field moves by badge in src/party_menu.c

milestones.name: Team Rocket in Mt. Moon
milestones.tips: Rocket grunts (Pokémon at 11-13) and the Super Nerd Miguel (Grimer, Voltorb, Koffing at 12) guard the fossils on B2F. Pick the Dome Fossil (Kabuto) or Helix Fossil (Omanyte).
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (MtMoon_B2F trainers)

milestones.name: Rival: Cerulean City
milestones.tips: At Cerulean's north exit: Pidgeotto 17, Abra 16, Rattata 15 and the starter at 18. Then the Nugget Bridge's five trainers and a Rocket.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (RIVAL_CERULEAN_*)

milestones.name: Gym 2: Misty
milestones.badge_note: Cascade Badge: Cut works in the field, and traded Pokémon up to Level 30 obey. Gym TM: TM03 Water Pulse.
milestones.tips: Staryu 18 and Starmie 21 (Water/Psychic, fast, Water Pulse). Grass and Electric moves: Bulbasaur, Pikachu from Viridian Forest, Bellsprout on Routes 24-25.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h; obedience in src/battle_util.c

milestones.name: Help Bill (Route 25)
milestones.tips: Bill is stuck as a Pokémon in his Sea Cottage at the end of Route 25. Help him and he gives you the S.S. Ticket for the ship in Vermilion.
milestones.source: pret/pokefirered Route25_SeaCottage scripts

milestones.name: The robbed house in Cerulean
milestones.tips: A Rocket grunt broke into a house; follow him out of the back and beat him (Machop, Drowzee at 17) to get TM28 Dig back. The way south then opens.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h; CeruleanCity scripts (TM28); pret/pokefirered CeruleanCity scripts (TRAINER_TEAM_ROCKET_GRUNT_5)

milestones.name: Rival: S.S. Anne
milestones.tips: On the ship's 2nd deck: Pidgeotto 19, Raticate 16, Kadabra 18 and the starter's middle form at 20. The captain then gives you HM01 Cut.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (RIVAL_SS_ANNE_*); SSAnne_CaptainsOffice (HM01)

milestones.name: Gym 3: Lt. Surge
milestones.badge_note: Thunder Badge: Fly works in the field (HM02 from a girl in a house on Route 16). Gym TM: TM34 Shock Wave.
milestones.tips: Voltorb 21, Pikachu 18, Raichu 24. Ground types are immune to Electric: Diglett from Diglett's Cave just east of Vermilion. Cut the tree in front of the gym; flip the two trash-can switches.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h

milestones.name: Rock Tunnel to Lavender Town
milestones.tips: Go north from Cerulean along Route 9 to Rock Tunnel. It is pitch dark without Flash (HM05). Lavender Town waits on the far side.
milestones.source: pret/pokefirered RockTunnel map (requires_flash)

milestones.name: Rival: Pokémon Tower
milestones.tips: Your rival waits on the tower's 2nd floor: five Pokémon, the starter at 25. The ghosts above can't be fought until you have the Silph Scope.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (RIVAL_POKEMON_TOWER_*)

milestones.name: Gym 4: Erika
milestones.badge_note: Rainbow Badge: Strength works in the field (HM04 from the Safari Zone warden), and traded Pokémon up to Level 50 obey. Gym TM: TM19 Giga Drain.
milestones.tips: Victreebel 29, Tangela 24, Vileplume 29. Fire, Flying, Ice, Poison and Psychic moves; watch for Sleep Powder and Stun Spore (bring Awakenings).
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h

milestones.name: Rocket Hideout under the Game Corner
milestones.tips: A poster in Celadon's Game Corner hides the stairs. The Lift Key is on B4F; Giovanni waits at the end with Onix 25, Rhyhorn 24 and Kangaskhan 29 and drops the Silph Scope.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (BOSS_GIOVANNI, RocketHideout_B4F)

milestones.name: Free Mr. Fuji (Pokémon Tower)
milestones.tips: With the Silph Scope, the ghost on 6F is Marowak (Level 30; it can't be caught). Three grunts (up to 26) hold Mr. Fuji on 7F; he gives you the Poké Flute, which wakes the Snorlax on Routes 12 and 16.
milestones.source: pret/pokefirered PokemonTower_6F (Marowak 30), 7F, MrFujisHouse scripts; ROM BPGE trainer table (PokemonTower_7F grunts)

milestones.name: Gym 5: Koga
milestones.badge_note: Soul Badge: Surf works in the field (HM03 in the Safari Zone's secret house). Gym TM: TM06 Toxic.
milestones.tips: Koffing 37 twice, Muk 39, Weezing 43. Psychic moves are best: Koffing and Weezing have Levitate, so Ground moves miss them. The gym's walls are invisible.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h

milestones.name: Rival: Silph Co.
milestones.tips: On 7F: Pidgeot 37, Alakazam 35 and three more with the starter's final form at 40. Ice, Electric and Rock moves for Pidgeot; Dark, Bug or Ghost for Alakazam.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (RIVAL_SILPH_*)

milestones.name: Giovanni at Silph Co.
milestones.tips: Bring the Tea (from an old woman in Celadon) to pass the Saffron guards. Find the Card Key on 5F; Giovanni waits on 11F with Nidorino, Kangaskhan, Rhyhorn and Nidoqueen 41. The president then gives you the Master Ball.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (BOSS_GIOVANNI_2, SilphCo_11F); SilphCo_11F (Master Ball)

milestones.name: Fighting Dojo (Saffron City)
milestones.tips: The dojo next to Saffron's gym: four Black Belts, then the master Koichi with Hitmonlee and Hitmonchan at 37. Psychic and Flying moves win. Afterwards take Hitmonlee or Hitmonchan (Level 25); only one.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered SaffronCity_Dojo scripts

milestones.name: Gym 6: Sabrina
milestones.badge_note: Marsh Badge: Rock Smash works in the field (HM06 on Kindle Road, One Island), and traded Pokémon up to Level 70 obey. Gym TM: TM04 Calm Mind.
milestones.tips: Kadabra 38, Mr. Mime 37, Venomoth 38, Alakazam 43. Bug, Ghost and Dark moves (Bite, Crunch, Shadow Ball); a Snorlax or Kangaskhan takes her Psychic hits well. Teleport tiles lead to her.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h

milestones.name: Gym 7: Blaine
milestones.badge_note: Volcano Badge: Waterfall works in the field (HM07 lies in Icefall Cave after the Hall of Fame). Gym TM: TM38 Fire Blast.
milestones.tips: Growlithe 42, Ponyta 40, Rapidash 42, Arcanine 47. Water, Ground and Rock moves. The gym door is locked: the Secret Key is in the Pokémon Mansion's basement. Answer the quiz machines to skip trainers.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h

milestones.name: One Island: the Ruby for Celio
milestones.tips: Bill takes you to One Island. Celio needs a gem for his network machine: go up Kindle Road to Mt. Ember, beat the two Rocket grunts (up to 37), solve the Braille room and take the Ruby. Two and Three Island open on the way.
milestones.source: pret/pokefirered OneIsland, MtEmber scripts; ROM BPGE (Mt. Ember grunts); pret/pokefirered MtEmber_Exterior (TEAM_ROCKET_GRUNT_43/44)

milestones.name: Find Lostelle (Berry Forest)
milestones.tips: On Three Island, bikers block the town; beat them. Lostelle, Two Island's girl, is lost in Berry Forest; a wild Hypno (Level 30) attacks you there.
milestones.source: pret/pokefirered ThreeIsland_BerryForest (Hypno 30)

milestones.name: Moltres (Mt. Ember summit)
milestones.tips: Moltres waits at Mt. Ember's summit at Level 50 once you can Rock Smash and Strength your way up. Water and Rock moves weaken it; Ultra Balls and a sleep move.
milestones.source: pret/pokefirered MtEmber_Summit (setwildbattle SPECIES_MOLTRES, 50)

milestones.name: Gym 8: Giovanni
milestones.badge_note: Earth Badge: every traded Pokémon obeys. Gym TM: TM26 Earthquake.
milestones.tips: Ground types: Rhyhorn 45 and 50, Dugtrio 42, Nidoqueen 44, Nidoking 45. Water, Grass and Ice moves; Electric does nothing. The gym opens after the other seven badges.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h; ViridianCity_Gym (TM26)

milestones.name: Rival: Route 22 before the League
milestones.tips: With eight badges your rival waits on Route 22 again: Pidgeot and Alakazam at 47, Rhyhorn, two more at 45 and the starter at 53.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (RIVAL_ROUTE22_LATE_*)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Lorelei
milestones.tips: Dewgong 52, Cloyster 51, Slowbro 52, Jynx and Lapras 54. Electric, Fighting, Rock and Steel moves; Lapras is tough, so save an Electric attack.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h

milestones.name: Elite Four: Bruno
milestones.tips: Two Onix (51, 54), Hitmonchan and Hitmonlee 53, Machamp 56. Water or Grass for the Onix, Psychic and Flying for the rest.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h

milestones.name: Elite Four: Agatha
milestones.tips: Gengar 54 and 58, Golbat 54, Haunter 53, Arbok 56. Psychic and Ground moves (but Gengar has Levitate); Ghost and Dark hit the Gengar line too.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h

milestones.name: Elite Four: Lance
milestones.tips: Gyarados 56, two Dragonair 54, Aerodactyl 58, Dragonite 60. Ice moves (four times on Dragonite), Electric for Gyarados, Rock or Water for Aerodactyl.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h

milestones.name: Champion: your rival
milestones.tips: Pidgeot 59, Alakazam 57, Rhydon 59, two of Gyarados/Arcanine/Exeggutor, and the starter's final form at 63. Cover Rock, Electric, Water and Ice; Alakazam is fast but frail.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (CHAMPION_FIRST_*)

milestones.name: National Pokédex
milestones.tips: After the Hall of Fame Oak upgrades your Pokédex to the national one once you own 60 species and have been to One Island. Johto Pokémon then appear in the Sevii Islands and Kanto's water.
milestones.source: pret/pokefirered PalletTown_ProfessorOaksLab scripts (60, FLAG_WORLD_MAP_ONE_ISLAND)

milestones.name: Sevii Islands 4-7: the Sapphire
milestones.tips: Celio now needs the Sapphire. Visit Four Island (Lorelei; Icefall Cave), find the Rocket Warehouse on Five Island, then the Dotted Hole on Six Island, where the scientist Gideon steals the Sapphire for the Rockets.
milestones.source: pret/pokefirered FourIsland, FiveIsland, SixIsland scripts

milestones.name: Team Rocket in Icefall Cave (Four Island)
milestones.tips: In Icefall Cave's back room Lorelei finds Rockets taking Pokémon. Beat the grunt (two Zubat and a Golbat at 38): Electric, Ice, Psychic or Rock moves. HM07 Waterfall is in the cave.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered FourIsland_IcefallCave_Back (TEAM_ROCKET_GRUNT_45)

milestones.name: Rocket Warehouse (Five Island)
milestones.tips: Grunts up to 49, the scientist Gideon (five Electric/Normal Pokémon at 46) and two admins: Muk, Arbok, Vileplume 54, and Golbat, Weezing, Houndoom 55. Ground, Psychic and Water moves cover them.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (FiveIsland_RocketWarehouse)

milestones.name: Articuno (Seafoam Islands)
milestones.tips: Push the boulders with Strength to slow the currents, then surf to Articuno on B4F (Level 50). Fire, Rock, Electric and Steel moves; it knows Mist and Agility.
milestones.source: pret/pokefirered SeafoamIslands_B4F (setwildbattle SPECIES_ARTICUNO, 50)

milestones.name: Zapdos (Power Plant)
milestones.tips: Surf down Route 10's river to the Power Plant. Zapdos waits deep inside at Level 50; some items there are Electrode (34) in disguise. Rock and Ice moves; a Ground type is immune to its Thunderbolt.
milestones.source: pret/pokefirered PowerPlant (Zapdos 50, Electrode 34)

milestones.name: Mewtwo (Cerulean Cave)
milestones.tips: Cerulean Cave opens once Celio's network is complete (both gems delivered). Mewtwo is on B1F at Level 70: save first, bring many Ultra Balls, or the Master Ball.
milestones.source: pret/pokefirered CeruleanCave_B1F (Mewtwo 70), OneIsland_PokemonCenter_1F (FLAG_HIDE_CERULEAN_CAVE_GUARD)

milestones.name: A roaming legendary beast
milestones.tips: After the National Pokédex one beast roams Kanto's routes at Level 50, chosen by your starter: Raikou for Squirtle, Entei for Bulbasaur, Suicune for Charmander. It flees at once; trap or sleep it.
milestones.source: pret/pokefirered src/roamer.c (species by starter, Level 50)

milestones.name: Elite Four rematch: Lorelei
milestones.tips: After the National Pokédex the Elite Four fight with stronger teams (Lorelei's top Pokémon at 66).
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (rematch teams)

milestones.name: Elite Four rematch: Bruno
milestones.tips: After the National Pokédex the Elite Four fight with stronger teams (Bruno's top Pokémon at 68).
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (rematch teams)

milestones.name: Elite Four rematch: Agatha
milestones.tips: After the National Pokédex the Elite Four fight with stronger teams (Agatha's top Pokémon at 70).
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (rematch teams)

milestones.name: Elite Four rematch: Lance
milestones.tips: After the National Pokédex the Elite Four fight with stronger teams (Lance's top Pokémon at 72).
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (rematch teams)

milestones.name: Champion rematch
milestones.tips: The rival's rematch team adds Heracross and Tyranitar; the starter's final form is at 75. Bug, Ground and Fighting moves for Tyranitar, Fire or Flying for Heracross.
milestones.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h (CHAMPION_REMATCH_*)

milestones.name: Trainer Tower (Seven Island)
milestones.tips: A timed climb through floors of preset trainers, alone or in doubles. Beat your best time for prizes from the owner at the top.
milestones.source: pret/pokefirered SevenIsland_TrainerTower scripts

steps.title: Pick a starter
steps.text: Bulbasaur makes the first two gyms easy; Squirtle is solid all game; Charmander struggles early but learns Metal Claw at 13 (good against Brock).

steps.title: Catch early helpers
steps.text: Viridian Forest has Pikachu (rare) and Caterpie, which becomes Butterfree with Confusion at 10. Routes 22 and 3 have Mankey for Brock.

steps.title: Flash needs ten species
steps.text: Oak's aide in the house on Route 2 (east of Viridian Forest's exit, through Diglett's Cave or a Cut tree) gives HM05 Flash once you have caught 10 species. Rock Tunnel is dark without it.

steps.title: Diglett's Cave
steps.text: Diglett's Cave links Vermilion to Route 2. Diglett is immune to Electric, which makes Lt. Surge easy.

steps.title: Itemfinder and VS Seeker
steps.text: Oak's aide on the 2nd floor of Route 11's gate gives the Itemfinder once you have 30 species. A woman in Vermilion's Pokémon Center gives the VS Seeker, which asks trainers on a route for rematches.

steps.title: Celadon Department Store
steps.text: TMs on 2F, evolution stones on 4F and drinks on the roof (Fresh Water, Soda Pop, Lemonade). A girl on the roof trades a TM for a drink. The old woman in Celadon Mansion gives the Tea for the Saffron guards.

steps.title: Silph Scope first
steps.text: The ghosts in Pokémon Tower can't be fought or caught without the Silph Scope from Giovanni in the Rocket Hideout.

steps.title: Snorlax with the Poké Flute
steps.text: Two sleeping Snorlax block Route 12 and Route 16. Play the Poké Flute to wake them; each is a Level 30 wild battle you can catch.

steps.title: Cycling Road
steps.text: Route 16 to 18 is Cycling Road down to Fuchsia; you need the Bicycle (Cerulean's shop, after the Bike Voucher from the Pokémon Fan Club chairman in Vermilion).

steps.title: Safari Zone: Surf and Strength
steps.text: Reach the secret house deep in the Safari Zone for HM03 Surf. The Gold Teeth there go back to the warden in Fuchsia, who gives HM04 Strength.

steps.title: Fly from Route 16
steps.text: Cut the tree beside Route 16's gate and a girl in the small house gives HM02 Fly (Thunder Badge).

steps.title: Secret Key in the Pokémon Mansion
steps.text: Surf to Cinnabar. Statues in the burned mansion flip switches that open and shut doors; the Secret Key for the gym lies in the basement.

steps.title: Revive your fossils
steps.text: Cinnabar's Pokémon Lab revives the Dome Fossil (Kabuto), Helix Fossil (Omanyte) and Old Amber (Aerodactyl) at Level 5.

steps.title: Rock Smash on Kindle Road
steps.text: A man at the Ember Spa on Kindle Road gives HM06 Rock Smash. Mt. Ember's way to Moltres needs it, plus Strength.

steps.title: Victory Road
steps.text: Boulder switches (Strength) open the way. The league has a Pokémon Center and Mart at Indigo Plateau, but no healing between the Elite Four.

steps.title: Elite Four plan
steps.text: Fought in a row: Ice, Fighting, Ghost, Dragon, then your rival. A team near Level 55-60 with Electric, Ice, Psychic and Ground moves and a bag of Full Restores and Revives.
steps.source: ROM BPGE trainer table; pret/pokefirered src/data/trainers.h

steps.title: Waterfall in Icefall Cave
steps.text: HM07 Waterfall is in Icefall Cave on Four Island; help Lorelei with the Rockets there. Waterfall opens the way to the rest of the Sevii Islands' secrets.

steps.title: Tanoby Ruins and Unown
steps.text: Seven Tanoby chambers on Seven Island's south coast hold the Unown forms. Solve the boulder puzzle at the Tanoby Key first; that opens all the chambers.

steps.title: Trade with Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald
steps.text: Once Celio's network is complete, you can trade with Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald: Hoenn Pokémon and the Hoenn starters come from there.

steps.title: Teachy TV and the help system
steps.text: After the old man in Viridian shows you how to catch a Pokémon, he gives you the Teachy TV with short lessons. Press L or R in most menus for the game's own help.

steps.title: The Game Corner's poster
steps.text: A Rocket grunt stands by a poster in Celadon's Game Corner. Beat him and press the switch behind the poster: the stairs to the Rocket Hideout open. On B4F a grunt drops the Lift Key, which runs the lift down to Giovanni.

steps.title: Card Key in Silph Co.
steps.text: Silph Co.'s doors are locked. The Card Key lies on 5F and opens them; Giovanni waits on 11F.
steps.source: pret/pokefirered item_ball_scripts.inc (SilphCo_5F Card Key), SilphCo_11F scripts

steps.title: Tri-Pass and Rainbow Pass
steps.text: On One Island Celio gives you the Tri-Pass for the ferry between One, Two and Three Island. Bring him the Ruby from Mt. Ember and he asks for one more gem and gives the Rainbow Pass, which reaches Four to Seven Island.

A salesman in the Pokémon Center at the foot of Mt. Moon (Route 4) sells a Magikarp for 500. It becomes Gyarados at Level 20.
Enter Celadon Mansion from the back and climb to the roof room: an Eevee (Level 25) sits in a Poké Ball.
On Silph Co. 7F an employee gives you a Lapras (Level 25) after you clear the floor.
Beat the Fighting Dojo next to Saffron's gym and take Hitmonlee or Hitmonchan (Level 25); you can only have one.
On Mt. Moon B2F the Super Nerd guards two fossils: Dome (Kabuto) and Helix (Omanyte). You get only one. Cinnabar's lab revives them.
The Pewter Museum's back room (reach it with Cut from the east) gives the Old Amber, which revives into Aerodactyl.
After the National Pokédex, an old man in the Water Labyrinth (Five Island) gives a Togepi Egg if your lead Pokémon is very friendly.
The Rocket grunt behind the robbed house in Cerulean returns TM28 Dig when you beat him.
Mr. Psychic's house in Saffron gives TM29 Psychic.
A little girl upstairs in Route 12's north gate gives TM27 Return.
Oak's aide in Route 15's gate gives the Exp. Share once you own 50 species.
Oak's aide in Route 16's north gate gives the Amulet Coin (double prize money) once you own 40 species.
A Soothe Bell lies on the top floor of Pokémon Tower (after Mr. Fuji is free).
The Macho Brace (double effort points while held) lies in Giovanni's gym in Viridian.
The Silph Co. president on 11F gives you the Master Ball after Giovanni.
A Metal Coat lies at the Memorial Pillar on Five Island (Onix and Scyther need it for a trade evolution).
A Dragon Scale lies on Six Island's Water Path (Seadra needs it to become Kingdra in a trade).
A King's Rock lies in Sevault Canyon on Seven Island (Poliwhirl and Slowpoke trade evolutions).
The Up-Grade for Porygon lies in the Rocket Warehouse on Five Island.
A Sun Stone (Gloom to Bellossom, Sunkern to Sunflora) lies in Six Island's Ruin Valley.
At the Memorial Pillar on Five Island, a mourning man rewards you with TM42 Facade for leaving Lemonade at the pillar.
The Game Corner prize room next door trades coins for Pokémon: Abra 120, Clefairy 750, Pinsir 2500, Dratini 4600, Porygon 6500 coins. Buy coins or find them on the floor.
A man in the Route 2 house trades his Mr. Mime for an Abra.
A Cerulean City house trades a Jynx for your Poliwhirl.
A Vermilion house trades a Farfetch'd (holding a Stick) for a Spearow.
At the Underground Path's north entrance (Route 5) a woman trades her Nidoran♂ for your Nidoran♀.
Route 11's gate (2nd floor) trades a Nidorino for your Nidorina.
Route 18's gate (2nd floor) trades a Lickitung for your Slowbro.
Cinnabar's Pokémon Lab has three trades: Electrode for Raichu, Tangela for Venonat, and Seel for Ponyta.
Several items in the Power Plant are Electrode (Level 34) in disguise.
Kanto's Safari Zone has Chansey, Kangaskhan, Tauros, Scyther and Dratini (Super Rod). You throw Safari Balls, bait or rocks; no battling.
Pattern Bush on Six Island is the place for Heracross; the Altering Cave there has only Zubat in the English game.
Lost Cave off Resort Gorgeous (Five Island) is a maze of look-alike rooms with Gastly and Haunter. Selphy's butler asks you to find her in it.
Berry Forest on Three Island is full of hidden berries; Drowzee and Exeggcute live there.
Cerulean Cave's wild Pokémon are the highest-level in Kanto (Ditto, Electrode, Kadabra, Chansey, Rhydon...).
Dotted Hole on Six Island: solve its Braille clue (Cut on the right spot) and go down to the Sapphire, where Gideon takes it from you. Catch him at the Rocket Warehouse.
Navel Rock (Ho-Oh and Lugia) and Birth Island (Deoxys) were opened by event tickets (Mystic Ticket, Aurora Ticket); normal play never reaches them.

evolutions.name: Kadabra
evolutions.text: Evolves only through a link trade (Game Link Cable or the Wireless Adapter; trades with Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald need Celio's network finished). Abra on Routes 24 and 25 (or the Game Corner) are the start.

evolutions.name: Machoke
evolutions.text: Evolves only through a link trade (Game Link Cable or the Wireless Adapter; trades with Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald need Celio's network finished). Machop in Rock Tunnel, Victory Road and Mt. Ember are the start.

evolutions.name: Graveler
evolutions.text: Evolves only through a link trade (Game Link Cable or the Wireless Adapter; trades with Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald need Celio's network finished). Geodude in Mt. Moon, Rock Tunnel and Victory Road are the start.

evolutions.name: Haunter
evolutions.text: Evolves only through a link trade (Game Link Cable or the Wireless Adapter; trades with Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald need Celio's network finished). Gastly in Pokémon Tower are the start.

evolutions.name: Poliwhirl
evolutions.text: A Water Stone gives Poliwrath; traded holding a King's Rock (Sevault Canyon) it becomes Politoed.

evolutions.name: Slowpoke
evolutions.text: Level 37 gives Slowbro; traded holding a King's Rock it becomes Slowking. Slowpoke lives on Route 12 and Four Island in LeafGreen.

evolutions.name: Onix
evolutions.text: Traded holding a Metal Coat (Memorial Pillar, Five Island) it becomes Steelix.

evolutions.name: Scyther
evolutions.text: Traded holding a Metal Coat it becomes Scizor. Scyther is FireRed-only; trade one in.

evolutions.name: Seadra
evolutions.text: Traded holding a Dragon Scale (Water Path, Six Island) it becomes Kingdra.

evolutions.name: Porygon
evolutions.text: Traded holding the Up-Grade (Rocket Warehouse) it becomes Porygon2.

evolutions.name: Eevee
evolutions.text: Fire, Water or Thunder Stone (Celadon Dept. Store 4F) for Flareon, Vaporeon or Jolteon. FireRed/LeafGreen have no clock, so Espeon and Umbreon cannot evolve here: trade Eevee to Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald.
evolutions.source: pret/pokefirered src/data/pokemon/evolution.h; src/pokemon.c (the day/night friendship checks are commented out)

evolutions.name: Golbat
evolutions.text: Evolves into Crobat on a level-up with high friendship (220). The Soothe Bell from Pokémon Tower speeds it up.

evolutions.name: Chansey
evolutions.text: Evolves into Blissey with high friendship. Chansey lives in the Safari Zone and Cerulean Cave.

evolutions.name: Pichu
evolutions.text: Pichu (from breeding Pikachu) evolves with high friendship; Pikachu then needs a Thunder Stone.

evolutions.name: Cleffa
evolutions.text: Cleffa (breed Clefairy) evolves with high friendship; Clefairy then needs a Moon Stone (Mt. Moon).

evolutions.name: Igglybuff
evolutions.text: Igglybuff (breed Jigglypuff) evolves with high friendship; Jigglypuff then needs a Moon Stone.

evolutions.name: Togepi
evolutions.text: The Togepi from the Water Labyrinth egg evolves into Togetic with high friendship.

evolutions.name: Gloom
evolutions.text: Leaf Stone gives Vileplume, Sun Stone (Ruin Valley) gives Bellossom. Oddish is a FireRed Pokémon: trade it in.

evolutions.name: Weepinbell
evolutions.text: A Leaf Stone evolves it into Victreebel. Bellsprout lives on Routes 24-25 and others.

evolutions.name: Nidorina
evolutions.text: A Moon Stone evolves it into Nidoqueen; Nidorino likewise becomes Nidoking.

evolutions.name: Nidorino
evolutions.text: A Moon Stone evolves it into Nidoking.

evolutions.name: Clefairy
evolutions.text: A Moon Stone evolves it into Clefable. Mt. Moon has the first stones.

evolutions.name: Jigglypuff
evolutions.text: A Moon Stone evolves it into Wigglytuff.

evolutions.name: Vulpix
evolutions.text: A Fire Stone evolves it into Ninetales.

evolutions.name: Growlithe
evolutions.text: A Fire Stone evolves it into Arcanine. Growlithe is FireRed-only: trade it in.

evolutions.name: Pikachu
evolutions.text: A Thunder Stone evolves it into Raichu. Pikachu lives in Viridian Forest and the Power Plant.

evolutions.name: Shellder
evolutions.text: A Water Stone evolves it into Cloyster. Shellder is FireRed-only.

evolutions.name: Staryu
evolutions.text: A Water Stone evolves it into Starmie.

evolutions.name: Exeggcute
evolutions.text: A Leaf Stone evolves it into Exeggutor.

evolutions.name: Tyrogue
evolutions.text: At Level 20: Attack higher than Defense gives Hitmonlee, lower Hitmonchan, equal Hitmontop. Tyrogue comes from breeding a Hitmon (Dojo gift) with Ditto.

evolutions.name: Magikarp
evolutions.text: Level 20 gives Gyarados. The Route 4 salesman sells one for 500.

evolutions.name: Dratini
evolutions.text: Level 30 gives Dragonair, Level 55 Dragonite.

evolutions.name: Abra
evolutions.text: Level 16 gives Kadabra, which then needs a trade.

evolutions.name: Machop
evolutions.text: Level 28 gives Machoke, which then needs a trade.

evolutions.name: Gastly
evolutions.text: Level 25 gives Haunter, which then needs a trade.

evolutions.name: Geodude
evolutions.text: Level 25 gives Graveler, which then needs a trade.

evolutions.name: Slowbro
evolutions.text: Slowbro does not evolve; Slowking comes from Slowpoke traded with a King's Rock.

evolutions.name: Kabuto
evolutions.text: Level 40 gives Kabutops; Omanyte becomes Omastar at 40.

evolutions.name: Sunkern
evolutions.text: A Sun Stone evolves it into Sunflora.

evolutions.name: Azurill
evolutions.text: Evolves into Marill with high friendship. In Gen III Azurill hatches from any Marill or Azumarill egg (no incense needed); Marill is a LeafGreen catch on the Sevii Islands.

evolutions.name: Wooper
evolutions.text: Level 20 gives Quagsire.

evolutions.name: Sneasel
evolutions.text: Sneasel does not evolve in Gen III (Weavile came later). It lives in Icefall Cave.

evolutions.name: Murkrow
evolutions.text: Murkrow does not evolve in Gen III (no Dusk Stone yet).

evolutions.name: Misdreavus
evolutions.text: Misdreavus does not evolve in Gen III.

evolutions.name: Larvitar
evolutions.text: Level 30 gives Pupitar, 55 Tyranitar. Larvitar lives in Sevault Canyon on Seven Island (rare).

notes.title: Only in LeafGreen
notes.text: Wild only in LeafGreen: Sandshrew, Sandslash, Vulpix, Bellsprout, Weepinbell, Slowpoke, Slowbro, Staryu, Magmar, Pinsir, Marill, Misdreavus, Sneasel, Remoraid, Mantine. Their evolutions follow.

notes.title: Trade from FireRed
notes.text: Wild only in FireRed: Ekans, Arbok, Oddish, Gloom, Psyduck, Golduck, Growlithe, Shellder, Scyther, Electabuzz, Wooper, Murkrow, Qwilfish, Delibird, Skarmory. Trade for them or their evolutions.

notes.title: Legendaries
notes.text: Articuno (Seafoam, 50), Zapdos (Power Plant, 50), Moltres (Mt. Ember, 50), Mewtwo (Cerulean Cave, 70) and one roaming beast (50). Snorlax twice (30). Mew, Lugia, Ho-Oh and Deoxys needed events.

notes.title: The roaming beast
notes.text: After the National Pokédex one beast roams Kanto: Squirtle's owner gets Raikou, Bulbasaur's Entei, Charmander's Suicune (all Level 50). It moves when you change routes and flees on its first turn.

notes.title: The Sevii Islands
notes.text: New to FireRed/LeafGreen: seven islands south of Kanto. 1-3 come with the main story (after the 7th badge), 4-7 after the Hall of Fame. They hold Johto Pokémon, the Trainer Tower and the Tanoby Ruins.

notes.title: Celio's network
notes.text: Trading with Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald needs both the Ruby (Mt. Ember) and the Sapphire (Dotted Hole, then the Rocket Warehouse) given to Celio on One Island.

notes.title: No clock
notes.text: FireRed and LeafGreen have no real-time clock: no day and night, no berry growth, and no Espeon or Umbreon by evolution.

notes.title: Physical or special by type
notes.text: In Gen III a move's type decides whether it is physical or special: Fire, Water, Grass, Electric, Ice, Psychic, Dragon and Dark are special; the rest physical.

notes.title: New since Red and Blue
notes.text: Abilities, natures, held items, Dark and Steel types, double battles and breeding all work here, so Kanto's old tricks change: Psychic is no longer unbeatable, and Koffing's Levitate dodges Ground.

notes.title: HM list
notes.text: Cut (S.S. Anne captain), Fly (Route 16 house), Surf (Safari Zone), Strength (Fuchsia warden), Flash (Route 2 aide), Rock Smash (Ember Spa, Kindle Road), Waterfall (Icefall Cave).

notes.title: In-game help
notes.text: Press L or R in most menus for the game's help screen; the Teachy TV shows short lessons. The Vs. Seeker (Vermilion's Pokémon Center) recharges as you walk.

notes.title: Game Corner Pokémon
notes.text: LeafGreen's prize room offers Abra 120, Clefairy 750, Pinsir 2500, Dratini 4600, Porygon 6500 coins. Coins can be bought or won at the slots.

notes.title: Starters' types
notes.text: Bulbasaur (Grass/Poison) becomes Venusaur, Charmander (Fire) Charizard (Fire/Flying), Squirtle (Water) Blastoise. The rival always takes the one with the type edge.

notes.title: Johto Pokémon after the National Dex
notes.text: After the National Pokédex, many Johto Pokémon appear: the Sevii Islands' routes, Kanto's water with the Super Rod, and caves. Johto starters and legendaries other than the beasts need trades.

notes.title: Two day cares
notes.text: The Route 5 day care only raises one Pokémon (it gains experience as you walk). Breeding needs the day care on Four Island, which takes two.

notes.title: Move tutors
notes.text: One-time tutors: Mega Punch and Mega Kick (Route 4), Seismic Toss (Pewter Museum), Rock Slide (Rock Tunnel), Substitute (Fuchsia), Double-Edge (Victory Road), Body Slam (Four Island), Explosion (Mt. Ember), Swords Dance (Seven Island) and more.

notes.title: Frenzy Plant, Blast Burn, Hydro Cannon
notes.text: An old woman in the house at Cape Brink (Two Island) teaches Venusaur, Charizard or Blastoise its strongest move if it is your lead and very friendly.

notes.title: Shiny odds
notes.text: A wild or gift Pokémon is shiny with a chance of 8 in 65,536 (about 1 in 8,192). Its colours show in battle and on the summary screen.
notes.source: pret/pokeemerald include/constants/pokemon.h (SHINY_ODDS, shared Gen III rule)

notes.title: Rematches
notes.text: The VS Seeker (Vermilion's Pokémon Center) shows which trainers on the current route want a rematch; it recharges as you walk. Rematch teams grow with your progress.

notes.title: Trainer Tower
notes.text: Seven Island's Trainer Tower has eight floors of preset trainers in single, double and knockout modes, timed. It is the postgame's battle facility.
